Enquiry 2: Athens vs Sparta — Where Would You Rather Grow Up in Ancient Greece? (c. 508–430 BC)

Big Question: How did democratic Athens and warrior Sparta govern their cities differently, and whose lives were freer in each polis?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Democracy (De-moc-ra-cy) Ostrakon (Os-tra-kon) Kleroterion (Kle-ro-te-ri-on) Metics (Met-ics) Agoge (A-go-ge)
TASK 1 Historical Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Inscribed Marble Portrait Bust of Athenian Leader Pericles (c. 430 BC Copy)
Democracy Clue: Elected strategos (general) by citizen vote on the Pnyx hill, Pericles led democratic Athens rather than ruling as a king.

1a. Why does Pericles wear a raised soldier's helmet instead of a king's crown in Source A?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A, Pericles wears a raised soldier’s helmet rather than a king’s crown because Athens..."
Word Bank: Pericles • strategos • citizen Assembly • no kings
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Golden Age citizens gather on the Pnyx hill and use stone kleroterion jury machines (c. 440 BC)
Cleisthenes establishes demokratia ("people power") in Athens (508 BC)
Sparta organises its strict agoge barracks system to train full-time hoplites (c. 650 BC)
Athenians scratch Cimon’s name onto ostrakon pot shards to banish him for ten years (461 BC)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events mattered most, and why?
